title: Open-Vocabulary Semantic Mapping and Hierarchical Reasoning for Long-Horizon Embodied Navigation in Unseen Environments
background:
Embodied navigation has advanced rapidly with the integration of vision-language foundation models, enabling agents to ground natural language instructions in 3D environments without relying on closed object taxonomies. Recent open-vocabulary approaches such as CLIP-Fields [1] and OpenScene-Nav [2] fuse 2D vision-language features into volumetric or implicit 3D representations, allowing zero-shot localization of arbitrary referents. In parallel, hierarchical exploration frameworks like HieroMap [3] decompose unknown spaces into rooms, regions, and frontier sets, achieving substantial gains in coverage efficiency over flat policies. For long-horizon instruction following, LLM-driven planners such as NavGPT-3 [4] decompose multi-step commands into subgoals and have demonstrated promising transfer on HM3D and ProcTHOR benchmarks.

Despite this progress, three fundamental gaps remain. First, current semantic maps suffer from feature drift and aliasing: CLIP-derived embeddings are view-dependent and noisy, leading to unstable object grounding under occlusion, lighting changes, or novel viewpoints [2][5]. Second, hierarchical exploration policies are typically trained or tuned on curated indoor datasets and degrade sharply in cluttered, multi-floor, or partially dynamic environments unseen at training time, with success rates dropping by 30-50% on out-of-distribution scenes [3][6]. Third, LLM-based planners lack tight coupling with geometric and semantic uncertainty: they hallucinate objects absent from the scene, fail to replan when subgoals become infeasible, and provide no calibrated confidence for downstream control [4][6]. Bridging perception, mapping, exploration, and language-conditioned planning into a unified, uncertainty-aware embodied system that generalizes to truly novel environments remains an open scientific challenge central to NSF's National Robotics Initiative and Foundational Research in Robotics priorities.
challenges: Constructing temporally consistent, open-vocabulary 3D semantic maps that resolve view-dependent CLIP feature drift and support fine-grained spatial relations (e.g., 'the mug behind the toaster') under partial observability

Designing hierarchical exploration policies that jointly optimize information gain, language-conditioned relevance, and traversability, while transferring zero-shot to unseen multi-room and multi-floor layouts
Tightly coupling LLM-based long-horizon planners with geometric and semantic uncertainty estimates to detect infeasible subgoals, suppress object hallucinations, and trigger principled replanning
Establishing reproducible benchmarks and evaluation protocols that disentangle perception, mapping, exploration, and planning failures across diverse photorealistic and real-world unseen environments
